history.p: Hartmann started composing his overture in March 1844. It had its first performance at the memorial performance for the Danish sculptor Bertel Thorvaldsen on 9 April, but it was not planned as stage music. It was not until "Hakon Jarl" was revived in 1857 that he composed the entr'acte music which he chose to give the same opus number as the overture.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cloth with marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover inscribed: "I.P.E: Hartmann. / Ouverture / til / Hakon Jarl. / Op. 40." On the flyleaf in pencil: "A / 5.3 P1 / Opført i Stockholm Musikforening / d 7 Marts 1893 / opført d 14 Maj 1900 i Kjbh. M-F. / opført d 31 Okt. 2 Novbr 1895 i Musikforeningen / (Hartmann 100 Aars Fødselsdag)", which is incorrect, since Hartmann was born 14 May 1805. Written in brown ink. Paper: 18 staves. Later pagination in pencil. On p. 16 instrument designations are written in Hartmann's hand. At the end an extra folio has been added (pp. 45-46) on which Hartmann has written: "Ved Slutningen af 'Hakon Jarl's 4de Act spilles / Følgende bag Scenen / Replik: Einar: Og hjelpe Olaf til at fange dig / og i den høieste den værste Galge / Hakon: Det maa jeg høre!" followed by five bars for ob., cl., cla., cor., trb,; tb. and gong. The staves for ob. and cl. have later been cancelled in pencil. Beneath the music: "Der raabes: Hakon! Hakon!". In lower right-hand corner signed and dated: "I:P:E:Hartmann / d. 6 April 1844." Title page in the same hand as title page of the autograph score.
